extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A benchmark of 506 human-annotated image–instruction–response triplets for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models. Instructions require joint reasoning over embedded text and visual elements. The dataset covers eight visual scenarios: Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract, Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan; Hritik Bansal; Kai-Wei Chang; Nanyun Peng
extraction.citeAs: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, and Nanyun Peng. CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024. arXiv:2401.13311v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from six sources. Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract images were retrieved from LAION-5B using category-specific keyword searches through the CLIP-retrieval UI. Application Usage images came from Rico. Web Usage screenshots were collected by scraping website links provided by the Open WebText Initiative. Infographic images came from the InfographicVQA test set, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes images came from the STVQA and ESTVQA test sets. Images were shortlisted through manual or OCR-based filtering, annotated by the authors with new instructions and reference responses, and verified by MTurk workers and cross-group author review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Software Collection; Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from LAION-5B; UI screens from the Rico Dataset, which contains 66,000 distinct screens from 9,300 Android apps; screenshots of websites linked by the Open WebText Initiative; and test-set images from InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Existing VQA test-set images were reannotated with novel context-sensitive instruction–response pairs rather than their original text-recognition-focused questions and answers. Website content was captured as screenshots. Samples were categorized into eight visual scenarios and additionally annotated for information extraction and mathematical reasoning requirements.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract images underwent manual filtering for annotation suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, PaddleOCR detected image text, and the top 500 images with the highest word counts were selected as candidates, a subset of which was annotated. Incorrect samples identified during verification and low-quality samples identified through cross-group review were removed, leaving 506 instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors were divided into two groups, each responsible for four visual categories. They wrote an instruction and ground-truth response for each selected image. Instructions could be questions or imperative tasks, could vary in complexity, and had to require joint reasoning over textual and visual cues rather than reasoning over OCR text alone. MTurk workers verified each triplet, after which each author group reviewed the other group's samples. Samples were also annotated for information extraction and mathematical reasoning requirements. Separately, qualified MTurk workers wrote human-baseline responses, and three independent MTurk annotators judged each predicted response on a randomly selected 280-instance subset without being shown model identity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk was used for triplet verification, human-baseline response collection, and human evaluation of predicted responses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk verification found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and cross-group author review checked adherence to guidelines and removed low-quality samples. For predicted-response evaluation, majority vote among three independent annotators determined final acceptance. Automatic evaluation methods were compared against human judgments on 1,680 responses; GPT-4 achieved the highest reported correlation, with ROC-AUC 85.9 and Spearman correlation 0.71.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Dataset instructions and reference responses were authored by the paper's authors, affiliated with the Department of Computer Science at the University of California Los Angeles, USA. Human-baseline annotators were mainly from the US. MTurk workers verifying dataset triplets were mutually exclusive from workers used for the human baseline and response evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR was used for text detection and candidate-image filtering. In a separate synthetic-scaling experiment, GPT-4V generated instruction–response pairs for 200 candidate Miscellaneous Natural Scenes images using in-context demonstrations, including negative examples and explanations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark evaluates capabilities relevant to real-world applications such as interpreting text-rich public-space navigation scenes to assist visually impaired people and understanding memes. During collection, the authors aimed to ensure that images, instructions, and reference responses were not offensive to any social group. They acknowledge that multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguards and can hallucinate; they did not observe apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information in the analyzed model responses.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human-baseline annotators were mainly from the US. The authors acknowledge that linguistic diversity and writing style can vary across social groups, potentially affecting human-baseline performance and human evaluation. They recommend involving annotators from more diverse regions for more reliable evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Finding suitable images for joint text–visual reasoning is complex and requires heuristic OCR filtering and manual selection. MTurk workers found instruction–response creation time-consuming, making it difficult within a limited budget. Human response evaluation is expensive and difficult to scale. The authors identify limited regional diversity among human-baseline annotators and call for more geographically diverse evaluation. The separate synthetic-scaling experiment produced easier examples than the human-authored benchmark and may be affected by a GPT evaluator favoring responses to GPT-generated instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models and augmented language models, including zero-shot and few-shot evaluation, human-performance comparison, and fine-grained analysis across visual scenarios and reasoning tasks. To facilitate model development, the planned release provides reference responses for 100 validation samples and withholds reference responses for the remaining 406 samples. The validation subset contains 30 Miscellaneous Natural Scenes samples and 10 samples from each other category. Unless otherwise stated, paper results use the entire dataset.
